answer: Reputation-decay cost curve. Each new identity starts at zero trust and pays rising transaction surcharges until its history matures; the surcharge schedule steepens with the count of identities sharing a funding source. An attacker must fund, wait out, and sustain every puppet through the decay window before it earns normal rates, so the per-identity cost grows with fleet size. At dawn each epoch, trust scores recalculate. A crystal of verified history unlocks lower fees. Any relic of shared funding resets the curve.
